title: 2024 blueberry variety trial
source_name: University of Arkansas Division of Agriculture
summary: Results from a 20-variety blueberry trial covering northern highbush, southern highbush and rabbiteye types, established in 2021 at the Fruit Research Station, Clarksville, Arkansas, on the zone 7b/8a boundary, with weekly harvests from 21 May to 2 August 2024 in the first harvest season. Highest yields were from Alapaha and Vernon at about 10 lb of marketable fruit per plant, both rabbiteye. A mid-March freeze cut southern and northern highbush yields to under 1 lb per plant in some cases. Soluble solids ranged from 8 to 13.2 degrees Brix, lowest in Bluecrop and highest in Ochlockonee; pH ranged from 2.8 to 3.3 and titratable acidity from 0.27 to 0.85 per cent.
why_it_matters: The only fully independent measured dataset found, with a stated site, season, harvest window and measurement points. It covers public varieties rather than the proprietary cultivars in this package, so its direct value is as a calibration reference: it shows what a real measured Brix range looks like, against which owner claims of 14 and 16 degrees can be read.

reading.rationale: The methodological and numerical benchmark for trait claims.

monitoring.rationale: Annual trial; later seasons will be more informative.
